content: 1. The plasma concentration of sulbactam may increase due to inhibition of OAT1, as active secretion via OATP1 contributes significantly to its clearance. Close monitoring is recommended. Avoid or consider alternative drugs when co-administering with agents that inhibit OAT1. 2. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the plasma levels or effects of sulfasalazine by reducing its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely, as glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentration of BCRP substrates. 3. Sunitinib can increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting its metabolism. Caution is advised when co-administering with P-gp/BCRP inhibitors. Close monitoring is necessary. 4. Suvorexant may elevate the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Tacrolimus can increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing its metabolism. Caution is advised when co-administering with OATP1B1/OATP1B3 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 6. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of tacrolimus via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the plasma levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Talazoparib is a P-gp substrate, and co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. Monitor closely. 8. Tamoxifen may elevate the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Tazemetostat may reduce the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Tecovirimat may decrease the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 11. Telmisartan may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing its metabolism. Caution is advised when co-administering with OATP1B1/OATP1B3 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 12. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of telmisartan via other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Co-administration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate plasma concentrations of drugs that are substrates of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3. Monitor closely. 14. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the plasma levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma levels or effects of teniposide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the plasma levels or effects of tenofovir AF by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentration of BCRP substrates. 17. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of tenofovir DF by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentration of BCRP substrates. 18. Tepotinib may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. Monitor closely. 19. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of testosterone via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Tipranavir may elevate the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the plasma levels or effects of tolvaptan via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of topotecan via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentration of BCRP substrates. 23. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the plasma levels or effects of trabectedin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Trofinetide may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via other mechanisms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Trofinetide, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may elevate plasma levels of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3 substrates. Avoid co-administration with sensitive substrates. 25. Tucatinib may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. Monitor closely. 26. Ulipristal may elevate the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Vadadustat may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via other mechanisms. Vadadustat may also increase exposure to BCRP substrates. Monitor for adverse effects of BCRP substrates and reduce substrate doses as per product labeling. 28. Vandetanib may elevate the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of velpatasvir via other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely, as glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentration of P-gp and BCRP substrates. 30. Vemurafenib may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing its metabolism. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may also elevate the plasma levels or effects of vemurafenib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Venetoclax may elevate the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may also increase the plasma levels or effects of venetoclax via the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Verapamil may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may also elevate the plasma levels or effects of verapamil via the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of vinblastine via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma levels or effects of vincristine via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 35. Voclosporin may increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir via other mechanisms. Voclosporin, an OATP1B1 inhibitor, may elevate the concentration of OATP1B1 substrates. Monitor for adverse reactions of OATP1B1 substrates when co-administered with voclosporin. 36. Voriconazole may elevate the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the plasma levels or effects of voxilaprevir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant via other mechanisms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. OATP1B3 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to zavegepant, an OATP1B3 substrate. 39. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is metabolized by CYP3A4 (secondary pathway). Its half-life is approximately 6 hours for glecaprevir and 13 hours for pibrentasvir. 40. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir tablets should be taken with food at the same time once daily. Sprinkle oral pellets on a small amount of soft food with low water content (e.g., peanut butter, chocolate hazelnut spread, cream cheese, thick jam, or Greek yogurt) that adheres to a spoon and can be swallowed without chewing. Avoid liquids or foods that may cause the drug to dissolve quickly, as this may reduce its effectiveness. 41. Store glecaprevir/pibrentasvir tablets or pellets at or below 30°C (86°F). 42. There is no adequate human data to determine whether glecaprevir/pibrentasvir poses a risk to pregnancy outcomes. It is unknown if the drug is distributed in human breast milk. In lactating rodents, glecaprevir and pibrentasvir were present in milk without observed effects on the growth and development of nursing pups. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant from the drug or the underlying maternal condition.
